interviewQuestions.question: Explain write-through vs write-back caching, and when you'd pick one over the other.
interviewQuestions.answerMarkdown:
Write-through pushes every write to memory immediately — trivial consistency, but a write-heavy loop generates traffic on every write even if only the final value matters. Write-back keeps writes in the line, marks it dirty, writes to memory only on eviction — a thousand writes cost one eventual write, needing a dirty bit and careful eviction.

Most CPU caches default to write-back since programs write the same locations repeatedly. Write-through fits where simplicity matters more.

**Testing:** whether you connect the trade-off to *why* write-back dominates in practice.
interviewQuestions.subTitle: Write-through vs write-back
